currentContext.business: Established in 1991, Control Print manufactures and sells a diversified range of industrial coding and marking printers, the associated consumables, spare parts and after-sales services to corporate manufacturing customers across India and export markets. Its operations are anchored by a highly predictable, annuity-driven consumables model that generates more than 60% of consolidated revenue, with each printer installation compounding recurring demand for consumables, spares and service across a 7-8-year equipment lifecycle. Beyond the core, the Company operates a Track and Trace division built on its proprietary QRiousCodes platform, a Packaging division scaling V-Shapes single-dose packaging technology, and European subsidiaries in digital printing and end-of-line automation.

Consumables: Specially formulated inks and materials for scannability and environmental durability
International hardware: Codeology UK print and apply labellers and pallet labellers
Packaging: Co-packing services for single unit serving sachets

currentContext.strengths: Only indigenous ('Make in India') manufacturer among the leading players in India's coding and marking industry, manufacturing 7 different categories of printers - a cost and localisation advantage versus multinational competitors|Compounding installed base of over 22,000 printers that generates annuity consumables revenue accounting for more than 60% of consolidated revenue|Deeply embedded systems within customer production lines create predictable, compounding cash flows across a 7-8-year equipment lifecycle - high switching costs|Nationwide service moat: 350+ dedicated sales and service engineers covering 1,700+ cities and towns and 2,700+ pin codes, minimising customer downtime|In-house R&D teams with dedicated laboratory and testing facilities developing industry-specific hardware and consumables|Fully integrated in-house ecosystem for track-and-trace - hardware and vision, consumables, software and associated services developed and supported internally, unlike fragmented software providers|Backward and forward integration of the manufacturing footprint: Nalagarh and Guwahati plants plus a new Assam site, strategically located for logistics efficiency and regional tax advantages|Global technology access through the acquisitions and integration of Markprint BV, Codeology UK and CP Italy S.r.l., enabling faster adoption and localisation of digital printing, automation and packaging technologies
currentContext.strategies: Strengthen the core coding and marking business by compounding the installed base - the base was expanded to over 22,000 active printers across India during the year, with each installation deepening customer relationships and expanding recurring demand for consumables, spares and services.|Prioritise quality of growth over volume-led expansion, strengthening customer relationships and broadening the base for future recurring revenues.|Build the next engines of growth beyond the core: a 46,823 sq. m. manufacturing facility in Assam to support growing ambitions in packaging materials and allied businesses, enhancing supply chain efficiencies and strengthening the manufacturing ecosystem in the North East.|Advance the data value chain through QRiousCodes, a proprietary hybrid cloud-based track-and-trace platform, positioning Track and Trace as an important part of the future of the coding and marking industry rather than an adjacent offering.|Deliver the track-and-trace stack as a fully integrated in-house ecosystem - hardware and vision, consumables, software and associated services all developed, integrated and supported internally - as a differentiator versus fragmented software providers.|Scale the packaging business through V-Shapes single-dose packaging technology, laying the foundation for innovative single-dose packaging solutions while creating opportunities for greater localisation over time.|Use the international subsidiaries (Markprint, Codeology and other overseas operations) not merely for market access but for technology partnerships, specialised expertise and innovation pathways, and supply these advanced solutions to key customers in India as well as across European markets.|Operate the Middle East subsidiary as a dedicated channel to target coding and marking opportunities across the region, deploying the integrated portfolio from India and Europe.|Maintain disciplined capital allocation - balancing investment in emerging opportunities against preserving a robust balance sheet, healthy cash position and reaffirmed credit ratings.|Sectoral consolidation: continue to strengthen presence across high-volume industrial sectors and key economic drivers where the Company already has strong traction.|Control Print pays out through the year rather than in a single instalment: the Board declared an interim dividend of Rs 4 per equity share (40% of the Rs 10 face value) at its meeting on 29th January, 2026, paid on 16th February, 2026, and has recommended a final dividend of Rs 6 per equity share (60% of face value) for the year ended 31st March, 2026 subject to Members' approval, taking the total for the year to Rs 10 per equity share. The Company has voluntarily adopted a Dividend Distribution Policy under Regulation 43A of the Listing Regulations, published on its website. The Directors do not propose to transfer any amount to reserves, so retained earnings flow to Other Equity and are redeployed in the business rather than earmarked. Unpaid or unclaimed dividends are transferred to the Investor Education and Protection Fund in line with the 2016 Rules. Reinvestment is directed into the subsidiary structure - during the year the Company, through its wholly owned subsidiary Control Print B.V., subscribed to further equity of Markprint B.V. to raise that stake to 90%. The Company has not accepted any public deposits within the ambit of Section 73 of the Companies Act, 2013, and the Board's Report notes there was no one-time settlement with any bank or financial institution and no proceeding pending under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016. Governance of capital allocation runs through an Audit Committee whose recommendations were all accepted by the Board during the year, supported by a Risk Management Committee, a Nomination and Remuneration Committee, a Stakeholders' Relationship Committee and a CSR Committee, with an SAP-based internal financial control system subject to internal audit at both factories and branches.|Phased and strategically aligned transition towards alternative and renewable energy sources, balancing sustainability objectives against cost efficiency, with detailed cost-benefit assessments undertaken prior to implementation.|Active leverage of available government incentives and long-term power procurement arrangements to manage the cost implications of the energy transition.|Investment in energy-efficiency initiatives and deployment of advanced energy management systems to optimise consumption and offset potential increases in operational costs.|Strengthened regulatory monitoring and compliance mechanisms to remain aligned with evolving energy requirements.|Strengthening of the occupational health and safety framework through implementation of comprehensive safety programmes, in response to heavy-machinery and electrical-hazard exposure.|Focus on strengthening employee retention measures while continuing to attract new talent, following the increase in permanent-employee turnover during 2025-26.|Material responsible business conduct issues identified with reference to the Sustainability Accounting Standards Board (SASB) 2023-24 standards, maintained by the International Sustainability Standards Board under the IFRS Foundation - accessed 11th June, 2026.|Board gender diversity: females constitute 28.57% of the Board of Directors (Key Management Personnel, comprising the Company Secretary and Chief Financial Officer, at 0.00%).|Grievance redressal mechanisms in place for every stakeholder group - communities, investors, shareholders (via SEBI SCORES and the Smart ODR platform, administered with the Registrar and Transfer Agent), employees and workers (Employee Grievance Policy), customers and value chain partners.|BRSR disclosures made on a standalone basis for Control Print Limited; assurance/assessment not applicable for the reporting period as per SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/CFD/CFD-PoD-1/P/CIR/2025/42 dated 28th March 2025.|CSR is applicable under Section 135 of the Companies Act, 2013 and the Company has undertaken projects/programmes in accordance with its CSR Policy, with details annexed to the Board's Report.|Vigil Mechanism / Whistle Blower Policy giving employees and stakeholders direct access to the Chairperson of the Audit Committee, with the Company affirming no director or employee was denied access and no complaints were received during the year.|Formal policy for the prevention of sexual harassment of women employees under the 2013 Act, with no complaints received during the year, and compliance with the applicable provisions of the Maternity Benefit Act, 1961.|Stated commitment that operations are conducted so as to ensure safety of all concerned, compliance with statutory and industrial requirements for environment protection, and conservation of natural resources to the extent possible.
currentContext.expansion: The routed sections of this Annual Report carry limited explicit capex disclosure - no dedicated capex or capacity-expansion chapter, project cost schedule or commissioning calendar appears in the text provided. What the Board's Report does describe is expansion by portfolio and division rather than by plant. The Company continues to grow in the safety and hygiene segment, having expanded the portfolio of products offered in that segment on top of the masks business of earlier years. The Track and Trace division has developed new products and solutions and has established itself in the domestic market by securing orders from certain large pharmaceutical companies. In the Packaging Division, the Company is actively engaged in tapping the huge market potential by exploring customers for co-packing activities, apart from the sale of laminates and of packaging machines for producing single unit serving sachets. The Board's Report also notes there has been no change in the nature of business of the Company during the year. On the funding side, the Company has not accepted any public deposits within the ambit of Section 73 of the Companies Act, 2013, and the details of loans, guarantees or investments under Section 186 are left to the notes to the financial statements. The AGM Notice for the 35th Annual General Meeting (to be held on 23rd July, 2026 through VC/OAVM) carries a recommended final dividend of Rs 6 per equity share for FY2025-26, ratification of the Cost Auditor's remuneration for the financial year ending 31st March, 2027, and ratification of the Control Print Employee Stock Option Scheme 2025 as the sole employee stock option scheme, with no additional scheme to be introduced under that approval.
currentContext.mdna: India continued to stand out as one of the fastest-growing major economies during 2025-26, supported by resilient domestic demand, sustained infrastructure investments and robust manufacturing activity.|Industries increasingly prioritised automation, traceability, product authentication and regulatory compliance as supply chains became more interconnected and quality standards more stringent - shifts management says reinforced the relevance of Control Print's solutions.|Broad-based growth with strong traction across sectors such as pipes, food, dairy, cable and wire, and steel and metals.|The core flywheel - machine installation, then recurring consumables, service support and repeat business - creates predictable and compounding cash flows across a 7-8-year equipment lifecycle because the systems are deeply embedded in customer production lines.|Recurring revenue streams and healthy cash generation provide the stability to keep investing in strategic priorities while maintaining financial flexibility.|The Indian coding and marking industry is valued at approximately Rs 2,200 Crores and remains a highly consolidated market, with the top four players accounting for nearly 80% of domestic business; Control Print is the only Indian company within that leading group and has established an 18-20% share among organised players, and says it continues to outpace broader industry growth.|As regulatory frameworks tighten globally and pharmaceutical traceability mandates expand, QRiousCodes positions the Company to address growing demand for traceability, anti-counterfeiting and data analytics.|The acquisitions of Markprint and Codeology bring complementary diversification to the core business, extending the offering beyond traditional coding hardware into digital printing and end-of-line automation.

risks.risk: Energy transition cost and evolving energy regulation
risks.note: Identified in the BRSR as a material risk: transitioning to alternative or renewable energy sources may result in increased operational costs and could pose challenges in keeping pace with evolving energy regulations, thereby potentially affecting both profitability and regulatory compliance. Management is mitigating through a phased transition, cost-benefit assessments before implementation, use of government incentives and long-term power procurement arrangements, stronger regulatory monitoring, and investment in energy-efficiency initiatives and advanced energy management systems. The Company records no negative impact in the reporting period 2025-26.

risks.risk: Workforce health and safety in a heavy-machinery manufacturing environment
risks.note: Identified in the BRSR as a material risk: the use of heavy machinery and exposure to electrical hazards place employees at considerable risk of injury, and insufficient safety measures may result in workplace accidents leading to potential litigation, operational disruptions and elevated healthcare and insurance costs - impacting both financial performance and reputational standing. The Company says it is strengthening its occupational health and safety framework by implementing comprehensive safety programmes.

The BRSR turnover table shows the permanent-employee turnover rate rose in 2025-26 versus the prior two years, with the highest rate among female permanent employees; the Company explicitly notes it experienced an increase in turnover during the year and is focused on strengthening retention measures while continuing to attract new talent to meet business needs. Attrition matters for a business whose service moat depends on 350+ factory-trained sales and service engineers.

risks.risk: Concentration of the business in a single manufacturing activity line
risks.note: The BRSR shows the entity's turnover is dominated by manufacturing - printing and reproduction of recorded media at 84.51% of turnover, with the balance 15.49% from support services (rental and leasing of machinery, equipment and capital goods), and within products the manufacture of printing ink alone accounts for 61.00% of turnover contributed. Structural exposure is therefore concentrated in ink/consumables demand from industrial customers.

risks.risk: Thin export base against a stated international growth ambition
risks.note: Exports contribute only 2.46% of the Company's total turnover even though it serves 19 international countries across Asia, Africa, Europe and the Middle East; the international ambition rests on scaling through the wholly owned subsidiary Control Print MEA FZE, making execution of that channel a structural dependency rather than an established revenue base.

risks.risk: Reliance on the internal risk-management and internal-control framework in the absence of a granular disclosed risk register
risks.note: The Board's Report states that risk management involves reviewing operations, identifying potential threats and their likelihood, and taking appropriate action, with a Risk Management Committee that frames, implements and monitors the risk management plan and an Audit Committee holding additional oversight of financial risks and controls; major risks identified by businesses and functions are addressed through mitigating actions on a continuing basis. The Company does not enumerate its individual business risks in this report, so external visibility on specific structural exposures rests on that committee process, the SAP-based internal financial control system and internal audits at both factories and branches.

The BRSR complaints table shows customer complaints were resolved only post closure of the financial year, and of 4 shareholder complaints received in the prior year 2 were resolved during that reporting year while the remaining 2 were resolved on 9 April 2025 - a modest but recurring lag in grievance closure across stakeholder groups.

one-line thesis: Stand-alone revenue and profitability surged due to strong coding & marking demand and operational leverage, while V-Shapes Italy losses narrowed significantly; the company is now betting on two high-stakes pharma track & trace pilots and recyclable packaging material development to unlock next-phase growth.
financial scorecard: revenue: ₹202cr H1FY26 (+11.6% YoY); EBITDA/margin: 33.0% standalone (up from 31.8% H1FY25); PAT (rptd): ₹68.5cr H1FY26; PAT (normalized): ₹72.5cr H1FY26 (ex-₹4cr Q1 capital subsidy); order book: undisclosed but co-packing orders growing; net debt: net cash position (no debt mentioned, CapEx funded internally)
guidance: revenue growth: >15% YoY for standalone coding & marking; margin: sustain >33% standalone; order inflow: expect pickup in V-Shapes machine orders in H2FY26; capex/commissioning: minimal for coding & marking; ₹764cr CWIP for software and facility lease (no new plant capex planned)
order book & pipeline: No exact figure disclosed; co-packing orders in Nalagarh (50k–200k units) and Italy growing; machine orders pending due to technical delays in Italy
segment / subsidiary detail: Coding & Marking: 89% of revenue; Q2 mix: 14% printers, 60% consumables, 9% spares, 16% services; Track & Trace: breakeven, two large pharma pilots underway; Packaging: V-Shapes Italy H1 loss ₹9.5cr (target: ₹10–12cr full year); co-packing launched in India and Italy; Digital Printing: integrated into coding & traceability solutions
growth verticals / optionality: Recyclable packaging material (patent pending) to reduce cost and enable EU compliance; pharma track & trace platform adoption could become industry standard; co-packing as demand generator for machine sales
margins & cost dynamics: Gross margin: 59.9% consolidated, 60.2% H1FY25; EBITDA margin up due to higher consumables mix, lower SG&A growth, and laser printer sales; manufacturing cost stable at 3% of revenue; employee cost 16% in Q2 (down from 18% in Q1)
capex / expansion: Minimal for coding & marking (capacity sufficient); ₹764cr CWIP for SAP/BI software upgrades and advanced lease payments; no new manufacturing capex planned for next 1–2 years
capital allocation: Prioritizing R&D for recyclable packaging and track & trace tech; reinvesting profits into software and co-packing infrastructure; no dividend or buyback mentioned; no external fundraise planned
risks & watch-items: V-Shapes Italy turnaround delayed; pharma track & trace pilots fail to scale; recyclable material R&D stalls; co-packing margins erode under volume pressure; forex volatility on Italy operations
management quality / tone: Confident on standalone growth, pragmatic on international challenges; focused on execution of two pharma pilots; acknowledging co-packing as strategic marketing tool, not just revenue stream; transparent about Italy losses and R&D risks
non-obvious takeaways: Co-packing is not a side business — it’s a market-seeding strategy to convert hesitant buyers into machine customers; recyclable packaging patent (2044 expiry) is a longer-term moat beyond the machine patent (2036 expiry); ₹764cr CWIP is mostly software/lease, not physical assets

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Established in 1991, Control Print manufactures and sells a diversified range of industrial coding and marking printers, the associated consumables, spare parts and after-sales services to corporate manufacturing customers across India and export markets. Its operations are anchored by a highly predictable, annuity-driven consumables model that generates more than 60% of consolidated revenue, with each printer installation compounding recurring demand for consumables, spares and service across a 7-8-year equipment lifecycle. Beyond the core, the Company operates a Track and Trace division built on its proprietary QRiousCodes platform, a Packaging division scaling V-Shapes single-dose packaging technology, and European subsidiaries in digital printing and end-of-line automation.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- India continued to stand out as one of the fastest-growing major economies during 2025-26, supported by resilient domestic demand, sustained infrastructure investments and robust manufacturing activity.
- Industries increasingly prioritised automation, traceability, product authentication and regulatory compliance as supply chains became more interconnected and quality standards more stringent - shifts management says reinforced the relevance of Control Print's solutions.
- Broad-based growth with strong traction across sectors such as pipes, food, dairy, cable and wire, and steel and metals.
- The core flywheel - machine installation, then recurring consumables, service support and repeat business - creates predictable and compounding cash flows across a 7-8-year equipment lifecycle because the systems are deeply embedded in customer production lines.
- Recurring revenue streams and healthy cash generation provide the stability to keep investing in strategic priorities while maintaining financial flexibility.
- The Indian coding and marking industry is valued at approximately Rs 2,200 Crores and remains a highly consolidated market, with the top four players accounting for nearly 80% of domestic business; Control Print is the only Indian company within that leading group and has established an 18-20% share among organised players, and says it continues to outpace broader industry growth.
- As regulatory frameworks tighten globally and pharmaceutical traceability mandates expand, QRiousCodes positions the Company to address growing demand for traceability, anti-counterfeiting and data analytics.
- The acquisitions of Markprint and Codeology bring complementary diversification to the core business, extending the offering beyond traditional coding hardware into digital printing and end-of-line automation.

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: Gross margin: 59.9% consolidated, 60.2% H1FY25; EBITDA margin up due to higher consumables mix, lower SG&A growth, and laser printer sales; manufacturing cost stable at 3% of revenue; employee cost 16% in Q2 (down from 18% in Q1)

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Prioritizing R&D for recyclable packaging and track & trace tech; reinvesting profits into software and co-packing infrastructure; no dividend or buyback mentioned; no external fundraise planned

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The routed sections of this Annual Report carry limited explicit capex disclosure - no dedicated capex or capacity-expansion chapter, project cost schedule or commissioning calendar appears in the text provided. What the Board's Report does describe is expansion by portfolio and division rather than by plant. The Company continues to grow in the safety and hygiene segment, having expanded the portfolio of products offered in that segment on top of the masks business of earlier years. The Track and Trace division has developed new products and solutions and has established itself in the domestic market by securing orders from certain large pharmaceutical companies. In the Packaging Division, the Company is actively engaged in tapping the huge market potential by exploring customers for co-packing activities, apart from the sale of laminates and of packaging machines for producing single unit serving sachets. The Board's Report also notes there has been no change in the nature of business of the Company during the year. On the funding side, the Company has not accepted any public deposits within the ambit of Section 73 of the Companies Act, 2013, and the details of loans, guarantees or investments under Section 186 are left to the notes to the financial statements. The AGM Notice for the 35th Annual General Meeting (to be held on 23rd July, 2026 through VC/OAVM) carries a recommended final dividend of Rs 6 per equity share for FY2025-26, ratification of the Cost Auditor's remuneration for the financial year ending 31st March, 2027, and ratification of the Control Print Employee Stock Option Scheme 2025 as the sole employee stock option scheme, with no additional scheme to be introduced under that approval.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Only indigenous ('Make in India') manufacturer among the leading players in India's coding and marking industry, manufacturing 7 different categories of printers - a cost and localisation advantage versus multinational competitors
- Compounding installed base of over 22,000 printers that generates annuity consumables revenue accounting for more than 60% of consolidated revenue
- Deeply embedded systems within customer production lines create predictable, compounding cash flows across a 7-8-year equipment lifecycle - high switching costs
- Nationwide service moat: 350+ dedicated sales and service engineers covering 1,700+ cities and towns and 2,700+ pin codes, minimising customer downtime
- In-house R&D teams with dedicated laboratory and testing facilities developing industry-specific hardware and consumables
- Fully integrated in-house ecosystem for track-and-trace - hardware and vision, consumables, software and associated services developed and supported internally, unlike fragmented software providers
- Backward and forward integration of the manufacturing footprint: Nalagarh and Guwahati plants plus a new Assam site, strategically located for logistics efficiency and regional tax advantages
- Global technology access through the acquisitions and integration of Markprint BV, Codeology UK and CP Italy S.r.l., enabling faster adoption and localisation of digital printing, automation and packaging technologies

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: V-Shapes Italy turnaround delayed; pharma track & trace pilots fail to scale; recyclable material R&D stalls; co-packing margins erode under volume pressure; forex volatility on Italy operations

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: Co-packing is not a side business — it’s a market-seeding strategy to convert hesitant buyers into machine customers; recyclable packaging patent (2044 expiry) is a longer-term moat beyond the machine patent (2036 expiry); ₹764cr CWIP is mostly software/lease, not physical assets

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Strengthen the core coding and marking business by compounding the installed base - the base was expanded to over 22,000 active printers across India during the year, with each installation deepening customer relationships and expanding recurring demand for consumables, spares and services.
- Prioritise quality of growth over volume-led expansion, strengthening customer relationships and broadening the base for future recurring revenues.
- Build the next engines of growth beyond the core: a 46,823 sq. m. manufacturing facility in Assam to support growing ambitions in packaging materials and …
